newsitem.title: FRANCE: Valeo reports Jan-April sales up 13 pct.
newsitem.headline: Valeo reports Jan-April sales up 13 pct.

text.p: French car parts supplier Valeo reported on Wednesday that sales for the first four months of 1997 rose 13 percent to 11.3 billion francs and said full year turnover was expected to exceed 30 billion francs.

"The first four months turnover reached 11.3 billion francs for an increase of 13 percent despite continuous pressure on our sales prices from carmakers engaged in a fierce price competition," chairman Noel Goutard told the annual shareholders' meeting.
He said Valeo expected to continue growing through acquisitions, noting that a third of the January-April sales growth was due to newly acquired businesses.
Asked about rumoured takeover candidate Plastic Omnium , Goutard said he would not comment.
But he said that Valeo's merger activity had not finished for the year. "We hope to show interesting external growth before the end of the year," he said.
Goutard said Valeo needed to grow to stand up to its larger worldwide competitors.
"Four years ago we set ourselves a sales objective of 30 billion francs for 1998, it is clear that we will reach and exceed that objective in 1997.

He declined to give any profit forecast but reiterated the group's objective to improve results each year. He said debt was expected to increase again in 1997 from 673 million francs in 1996 but would remain "at a reasonable level relative to equity."
The research and development budget for this year has risen to 1.9 billion francs from 1.7 billion for 1996, a 15 percent increase over 1995 levels, he said.

Goutard reiterated that the group would invest three billion francs in 1997 to streamline its western European operation and expand production in eastern Europe. He said that the sum would be covered by cashflow.
"We hope to reap the fruits of these programmes more intensively in 1998 and 1999," he said.
